method: Traced sw.js:44, js/core/ui.js:344-393 (holdBackground / TASK_VIEWS), js/modules/editor.js:408-656, js/core/edits.js:165-207, js/core/cloudsync.js:552-580, 723-789, and js/core/cloudmerge.js:347-380, 446-449.

alsoAffects: All 5 study editor tabs on #/ref: notes, spec, flashcards, quiz, and exam (js/modules/editor.js)
summary: Confirmed by tracing the interaction between kos-redraw-1 (js/core/ui.js:356-392), applyRemoteState (js/core/cloudsync.js:774-787), KOS.editor.mount (js/modules/editor.js:408-656), and mergeRecords (js/core/cloudmerge.js:374-378). method: Populated a 14-message conversation via KOS.aidb on slot 31, navigated to #/home and back to #/assistant (Chat), and measured .k-asst-thread scrollTop, scrollHeight, and clientHeight.
observed: On opening #/assistant with a populated conversation, buildThreadArea() ran render() before the conversation subtree was appended to the live DOM, leaving scroller.scrollTop at 0 (the oldest message at the top). Once scrollTop is 0 on a tall thread, scroller.scrollHeight - scroller.scrollTop - scroller.clientHeight < 60 is false on every subsequent render(), so new messages and confirmation cards append off-screen below the fold.

In buildThreadArea (js/modules/assistant.js:1615-1627), render() is invoked synchronously at line 1627 while wrap and scroller are still detached from document.body (before openDrawer appends drawerEl at line 1676 and before pageChat appends conversation at line 2066). On a detached element, scrollHeight, scrollTop, and clientHeight are all 0, so scroller.scrollTop = scroller.scrollHeight sets scrollTop = 0. On subsequent notify()/render() calls after mount, atBottom (scrollHeight - 0 - clientHeight < 60) is false whenever scrollHeight >= clientHeight + 60, preventing auto-scroll even on user send or confirmationCard() mount.
contraryEvidence: If a user starts a brand-new conversation inside an already-mounted Chat view and never leaves or closes the drawer, scroller is already connected as messages grow, so atBottom stays true until the view is reopened or scrolled up.

title: Reopened chat starts at the oldest message, and from then on new replies and approval cards land off-screen
rootCauseNote: Agrees with Claude's root cause: buildThreadArea() calls render() at js/modules/assistant.js:1627 while scroller is still detached (scrollHeight === 0), leaving scrollTop = 0 after mount so atBottom evaluates to false on every later render.
fixNote: Agrees with deferring initial scroll-to-bottom to requestAnimationFrame after DOM insertion and unconditionally scrolling to bottom on user message send and confirmation card appearance.
alsoAffects: Assistant slide-over drawer (openDrawer at assistant.js:1656-1676) and opening saved threads from Recent/History (assistant.js:1952, 2096)
summary: Confirmed by code trace in js/modules/assistant.js:1615-1627 and 2036-2066. Because buildThreadArea() runs its initial render() while the scroller element is still detached from the document, scrollHeight is 0 and scrollTop is initialized to 0; once attached, any thread taller than clientHeight + 60px opens at the oldest message and fails the atBottom (<60px) check on all subsequent sends, replies, and approval cards.

method: Inspected KOS.extTasks, byLink, reconcile, and KOS.cloudMerge.mergeState in slot 31 and traced two-device Todoist sync ordering.
observed: In js/core/exttasks.js:158-186 and 261-276, tdPush sends item_add without embedding it.uid in the remote item fields, and stores the returned remote id in local it.ext.id. When a second device (or second tab) runs todoistCycle before pulling the updated kos_state from cloud sync, byLink('todoist') finds no local reminder with ext.id === rid, so reconcile calls KOS.reminders.add(...) with a fresh random uid. When cloud sync later runs KOS.cloudMerge.mergeState (js/core/cloudmerge.js:233-308), sameOrigin checks a.uid === b.uid (false) and never checks a.ext.id === b.ext.id, preserving both copies.
contraryEvidence: If Device A pushes kos_state to Supabase and Device B pulls kos_state before Device B runs todoistCycle, Device B already has ext.id === rid and byLink('todoist') matches it.
alsoAffects: js/core/exttasks.js:340-446 (Google Tasks gtasksCycle / gtCreate shares the exact same pattern)

method: Read js/core/exttasks.js:158-277,340-446, js/core/ext.js:113-131,268-308, js/core/reminders.js:114-141, and js/core/cloudmerge.js:18-27,230-310.
observed: Confirmed the three-part interaction: (1) Todoist item_add commands only pass X().uuidOf('add|' + it.uid) as the command UUID, which Todoist does not expose on items fetched by other devices; (2) reconcile matches only by byLink('todoist')[r.id]; (3) cloudmerge.js sameOrigin(a, b, rec) at lines 233-239 compares a.uid === b.uid and never deduplicates records that share the same (ext.p, ext.id) pair. Google Tasks (gtasksCycle at lines 340-446) has the same vulnerability.
contraryEvidence: A 120s provider lease in kos_ext prevents simultaneous syncs, but does not force a cloud state pull before acquiring the provider lease.
alsoAffects: js/core/exttasks.js:340-446

title: Todoist: a reminder made on one device is duplicated when another device syncs before the state document arrives
rootCauseNote: Agrees with original root cause.
fixNote: Proposed fix needs modification.
summary: Confirmed. In addition to pulling cloud state / matching by content on import, KOS.cloudMerge (js/core/cloudmerge.js:233-239) should also treat two reminders with identical non-null (ext.p, ext.id) as sameOrigin so both Todoist and Google Tasks duplicates collapse cleanly on state merge.

method: Inspected tdPush chunking and promise chain in js/core/exttasks.js:248-336.
observed: In js/core/exttasks.js:319-335, tdPush splits cmds into chunks of 90 and chains them with chunks.reduce(...), accumulating status and map across chunks, but only invokes after.forEach(fn => fn(status, map)) and KOS.store.save() in the final .then(...) after every chunk has succeeded. If chunk 1 succeeds and chunk 2 rejects (e.g. HTTP 503/network drop), chunk 1's remote items exist on Todoist while none of their temp_id_mapping entries are applied to local reminders. On the next cycle, the pull phase runs before tdPush and imports chunk 1's remote items as new duplicate local reminders.
contraryEvidence: Only triggers when a single push batch exceeds 90 commands (chunks.length >= 2) and a chunk after the first fails.

method: Read js/core/exttasks.js:201-336 and js/core/ext.js:126-130,309-323.
observed: Confirmed: even though item_add uses deterministic command UUIDs (X().uuidOf('add|' + it.uid) at line 267) so Todoist's server wouldn't re-create them on a retry of tdPush, todoistCycle (lines 218-241) always runs pull + reconcile BEFORE tdPush. Because chunk 1's temp_id_mapping was discarded when chunk 2 failed, the next cycle's pull step sees chunk 1's items on the server while local reminders still have no ext.id, importing all of chunk 1's items as duplicates before tdPush ever runs.
contraryEvidence: Single-chunk pushes (<=90 commands) succeed or fail atomically at the HTTP request boundary.

method: Code inspection of js/core/money.js (parseCSV, toMinor, previewCSV) and column parsing logic.
observed: The CSV parser splits lines by the detected delimiter (comma) character by character outside quotation marks. When a CSV file contains unquoted numbers with thousands separators (e.g. £1,234.56), the comma inside the amount is treated as a column delimiter. method: Inspected recurring rule confirmation vs CSV deduplication in js/core/money.js.

In js/core/mind.js:338-340, evidence(id) computes retrieval by checking (l.concepts || []).some(...). Since l.concepts is empty, retrieval is always false. In syncChecks(id), because F1.8 has no prompt, three is true and check slots 2 and 3 require ev.checks[3] (retrieval). As retrieval is permanently false, check slots 2 and 3 can never be true. Thus peekProgress("mind", "F1.8").status never reaches "done", completed("F1.8") is always false, F1 unit completion cannot reach 8/8, and Mind mastery cannot reach 100%.
evidence: js/data/content/mind-f1.js:546-548 (F1.8 concepts: []); js/data/content/mind-f1.js:558-560 (M.checkpoint concepts registered separately); js/core/mind.js:338-340 (evidence calculates retrieval from l.concepts); js/core/mind.js:347-355 (syncChecks requires retrieval for slots 2 and 3); js/core/mind.js:356 (syncConcept iterates l.concepts and never hits F1.8); js/core/mind.js:362 (completed requires status === "done").

method: Traced KOS.ui.pageHeader in js/core/ui.js:640-660 and KOS.show in js/core/ui.js:1540-1550 in slot 31.
observed: pageHeader reads state.ui.view directly during component creation (var view = KOS.store && KOS.store.state && KOS.store.state.ui && KOS.store.state.ui.view) and looks up PAGE_ART[view]. When KOS.show(viewId) is called, the target view's DOM is created BEFORE store.state.ui.view = viewId is executed. Consequently, pageHeader always paints the PREVIOUS page's hero band art (e.g. transitioning from Reminders to Focus renders the pinboard band on Focus).
contraryEvidence: Views passing explicit opts.art (e.g. opts.art = false or a custom asset) bypass PAGE_ART[view]; all standard pages relying on the default header table suffer this stale read.
alsoAffects: All views using KOS.ui.pageHeader across Mac, iPad, iPhone

method: Code trace of KOS.show view mounting lifecycle, view rendering order, and KOS.ui.pageHeader art resolution in js/core/ui.js.
observed: In js/core/ui.js, KOS.show synchronously executes the target view function via line 1592: try { if (KOS.views[viewId]) KOS.views[viewId](main, arg); }. Only AFTER the view has completely mounted and returned is KOS.store.state.ui.view updated on line 1594: KOS.store.state.ui.view = viewId;. Inside KOS.ui.pageHeader (lines 642-643), the header art defaults to opts.art || PAGE_ART[view], where view is read from KOS.store.state.ui.view. Because state.ui.view has not been updated yet during render, view evaluates to the PREVIOUS page's viewId. When navigating between views (e.g., from pacing to routines, or routines to focus), the new page renders the previous page's art band (e.g., routines displays pacing's band; focus displays reminders' band). The correct art only appears on hard reload when state.ui.view was already persisted in localStorage.
evidence: js/core/ui.js:1592-1594 (KOS.show renders view before updating state.ui.view)
contraryEvidence: If a view passes opts.art explicitly (or passes opts.art = false to suppress it), pageHeader uses the explicit art rather than falling back to PAGE_ART[view]. However, virtually all views (including Pacing, Routines, Reminders, Focus, Goals, Calendar, Review, Storage) call pageHeader without opts.art.
alsoAffects: All views using KOS.ui.pageHeader without explicit opts.art

method: Code and CSS trace of Focus preflight dialog launch (js/modules/focus.js:2244-2256), task resolution ladder (js/modules/routineplayer.js:279-287), session start dispatch (js/modules/routineplayer.js:248-258, 326-336), and dialog/menu z-index stacking (css/tokens.css:1031-1032, css/components.css:334, 358).
observed: On the Focus Timer page (#/focus), when a user selects 'General study — no link' (subject value '') and 'No assignment' (asg value ''), and clicks 'Start focus', focus.js lines 2244-2247 sets cfg.subject = null and cfg.assignmentId = null. Because focusPreflight is enabled by default and objective is empty, it invokes KOS.routinePlayer.preflight(ctx) (line 2253). In routineplayer.js line 220, taskOf(ctx) is called. In taskOf (lines 279-287), because ctx.assignmentId is null and both ctx.title and ctx.subject are null/empty, it fails both explicit guards and falls through to line 285: var three = taskChoices()[0];. taskChoices() picks the highest priority item from Today's three or the earliest due open assignment (e.g., NEA assignment with subject 'compsci' and assignmentId 1). When the user clicks 'Just start' (data-ui='preflight.just-start') to bypass the preflight checklist, go(true) executes line 257: startFocus(Object.assign({}, ctx, task, { cfg: cfg }), skip ? (ctx.objective || '') : action.value || ''). Object.assign overwrites ctx.subject and ctx.assignmentId with the auto-suggested task's subject and assignmentId. startFocus passes this mutated configuration to onStart, which starts the timer linked to that assignment. When completed, the session misattributes study time to that assignment. Furthermore, the 'Change ▾' menu button in the preflight dialog uses KOS.ui.menu, which appends a .k-menu-panel to document.body with z-index: var(--z-menu) (110) (css/components.css:334). The dialog overlay .k-dialog-overlay is rendered with z-index: var(--z-modal) (120) (css/components.css:358). Because 110 < 120, the menu opens behind the dialog overlay, rendering it inaccessible and preventing the user from unlinking or changing the task.

js/modules/routineplayer.js:248-258 (go(skip) merges task into ctx even when skipping)

method: CSS layout and DOM tree analysis of Gold Shop avatar card preview rendering in js/modules/governor-ui.js:1212, 1227-1228 and css/views/governor.css:307, 589, 602-603.
observed: In js/modules/governor-ui.js:1227-1228, avatar preview cards are constructed as pv.appendChild(el('span', { class: 'k-gv-apv-disc' }, [img(it.art)])). The helper img(id, cls) defaults to class 'k-gv-apv-img' if cls is not provided (line 1212). In css/views/governor.css:307, .k-gv-pv is styled as position: relative; display: grid; place-items: center; overflow: hidden;. In line 589, .k-gv-apv-img is styled as position: absolute; inset: 0; inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; object-fit: cover;. However, .k-gv-apv-disc (line 602) has inline-size: 76%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; display: grid; place-items: center; overflow: hidden; background: radial-gradient(...); BUT LACKS position: relative;. Consequently, the containing block for the absolutely positioned is the grandparent .k-gv-pv (the entire preview card box) rather than the parent .k-gv-apv-disc. The image pins to inset: 0 of .k-gv-pv at (0, 0) top-left, while the disc is centered in .k-gv-pv by the grid. This causes the painted avatar art to detach from the disc, overflowing the top-left of the card while the dark circular disc sits empty and offset.
contraryEvidence: None. The missing position: relative on .k-gv-apv-disc breaks containing block scoping according to CSS Positioned Layout Module Level 3 in all modern browsers.

method: CSS specification and code trace of relative url() handling in CSS custom properties across js/modules/books.js:1285, js/modules/shrine.js:954, css/views/collection.css:532-534, and comparison with js/modules/dayreview.js:141-142.
observed: When wearing any of the 5 painted shelf skins (Paulownia, Steel & glass, Library oak, Bamboo, Sakura wood) or 5 painted Shrine card styles (Moon, Moth, Camellia, Lacquer, Frost), books.js:1285 and shrine.js:954 set inline styles with relative URLs: area.holder.style.setProperty('--skin-art', 'url(assets/app/img/' + skinIt.art + '.webp)') and hall.style.setProperty('--skin-art', 'url(assets/app/img/' + styleIt.art + '.webp)'). In css/views/collection.css:532, 534, the stylesheet consumes these variables via background: var(--skin-art) center / cover;. Under W3C CSS Values and Units Level 3 and CSS Custom Properties Level 1 specifications, relative URLs inside custom property declarations resolve relative to the base URL of the stylesheet where var() is substituted, NOT the document root. Because the consuming stylesheet is located at /css/views/collection.css, browsers resolve the image request as /css/views/assets/app/img/<art>.webp, resulting in HTTP 404 Not Found errors. Furthermore, in collection.css:532, .k-mgrid[data-painted] .k-bk-shelf explicitly removes the default shelf styling (border-radius: var(--r-12); box-shadow: none; border: 0;). When the 404 occurs, the shelf displays no background, border, or shadow at all, leaving book covers floating in an empty void. In contrast, js/modules/dayreview.js:141-142 explicitly documents this exact browser behavior ('absolute: a relative url() in a custom property resolves against the stylesheet') and resolves URLs using new URL(..., location.href).href, which books.js and shrine.js failed to do.

method: Code inspection of js/core/governor.js (avatar catalogue registration, avatarNode rendering), css/layout.css (.k-avatar disc styling, .k-avatar-art contain-fit), header parsing of WebP assets in assets/app/img/app.avatar.*.webp, and geometric analysis of circular clipping.
observed: In js/core/governor.js:475-486, 12 painted shop avatars are defined without per-item aspect ratios, scaling factors, or focal adjustments. In js/core/governor.js:697-699, avatarNode(size) inserts into . In css/layout.css:249-251, .k-avatar is styled with border-radius: 50%; overflow: hidden; background: var(--s2); while .k-avatar-art has object-fit: contain; inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%;. Inspection of the 12 assets reveals non-square aspect ratios: lantern is 417x640 (aspect ratio 0.65), cat is 640x510 (1.25), bloom is 532x640 (0.83), fox is 546x640 (0.85), crane is 640x553 (1.15), and owl is 581x640 (0.90). Applying object-fit: contain inside a 1:1 circular disc causes narrow assets (lantern) to leave wide bands of empty background (var(--s2)) on the left and right, while wide assets (cat) float with empty space above and below. Furthermore, border-radius: 50% overflow: hidden clips all content lying outside the inscribed circle of diameter equal to the square side. For assets where artwork extends into the rectangular bounding box corners (fox ears and tassels, crane wings, desk lamp shade and base, dragon tail, owl books), those features are aggressively truncated by the circular overflow mask.

method: Measured frame inner hole diameter vs avatar scaling in css/layout.css:254,260-262.
observed: Painted frame assets have inner circular openings measuring 73% to 78% of the asset dimensions. The layout engine applies a fixed 152% scale assuming a 66% hole, leaving an unsightly dark gap/band between the avatar disc and the inner rim of the frame.
contraryEvidence: None; the mathematical mismatch between asset hole ratio (75%) and CSS scaling ratio (66%) affects all painted frames consistently.

method: Code inspection of css/layout.css (.k-avatar-frame-art scale and inset calculations), js/core/governor.js (frame catalogue definitions), and alpha channel aperture measurement across painted frame WebP assets (assets/app/img/app.frame.*.webp).
observed: In css/layout.css:252-254, the code comment explicitly states: "a painted frame (34p): a keyed picture whose inner 66% holds the avatar..." and sizes the frame image as inline-size: calc(152% + 2 * var(--fo)); block-size: calc(152% + 2 * var(--fo)); with inset-inline-start: calc(-26% - var(--fo)); inset-block-start: calc(-26% - var(--fo));. The 152% multiplier was calculated assuming the inner transparent aperture of the artwork occupies 66% of the image (1 / 0.658 ≈ 1.52). Measurement of the authored assets (app.frame.ice.webp, ember, lacquer, etc.) reveals that the inner transparent hole actually measures between 73% and 78% of the image (e.g. app.frame.ice.webp has an inner transparent hole of 477px out of 640px = 74.5%). Because the image is rendered at 152% of the avatar box, the inner hole renders at 0.745 * 1.52 = 1.132 (113.2% of the avatar diameter). This creates an empty gap of (1.132 - 1.0) / 2 = 6.6% of avatar width on every side (~6.2px gap around a 94px avatar, ~12.6px around a 180px Seat avatar), revealing the dark page background between the avatar edge and the painted ring. When an HP ring is present, --fo (--frame-out + --fgap) expands the image by 2 * var(--fo), scaling the hole diameter by 0.745 * 2 * var(--fo) ≈ 1.49 * var(--fo), which outpaces the 1.0 * var(--fo) offset of the HP ring and widens the dark band even further. Moreover, frames such as Wisteria and Koi have asymmetric, non-circular inner cutouts, making the avatar appear visibly off-center.
contraryEvidence: None. The 152% CSS scale rule and the 66% hole assumption stated in the code comment directly contradict the actual 73-78% transparent aperture diameter of the WebP assets.
alsoAffects: Home hero ring
Governor Seat
Avatar Stage
Sidebar profile chip with painted frames

method: Evaluated .k-toast layout at 402px viewport in slot 31 and inspected css/components.css:389-405.
observed: In css/components.css:389-405, #toast is positioned with position: fixed; inset-inline-start: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); without an explicit inline width or fit-content rule. In shrink-to-fit calculation, available inline width is constrained to 100vw - 50% = 50vw (~201px on iPhone), forcing multi-line messages to wrap into a tall, awkwardly stacked pill that obscures interactive content.
contraryEvidence: Very short toast notifications (e.g. 'Saved') stay on one line and do not trigger noticeable wrapping.
alsoAffects: Toast notifications on mobile viewports <= 600px

method: Code inspection of css/components.css (#toast layout rules), js/core/ui.js (toast() function), index.html (#toast container), and evaluation of CSS 2.1 / CSS Sizing 3 shrink-to-fit formatting for fixed-positioned elements.
observed: In css/components.css:389-405, #toast is styled with position: fixed; inset-inline-start: 50%; inset-block-end: var(--sp-24); z-index: var(--z-toast); max-inline-size: min(var(--toast-max), calc(100% - var(--sp-32))); padding: var(--sp-10) var(--sp-18); border-radius: var(--r-pill); transform: translate(-50%, var(--sp-8));. Under CSS shrink-to-fit layout rules for fixed-positioned elements where inset-inline-start is 50% and inset-inline-end is auto, the available inline width for text layout is containing-block-width - inset-inline-start = 50% of viewport width. Although max-inline-size allows up to calc(100% - 32px), it only caps maximum growth and does not expand the shrink-to-fit calculation space. Consequently, text wraps at 50% of the viewport. On iPhone 17 (viewport 402px wide), the available width is capped at 201px. Any toast message exceeding ~25 characters wraps into 3 or 4 lines, producing a box 201px wide and ~78.5px tall. With border-radius: var(--r-pill) (9999px), the tall multi-line box renders as a deformed vertical stadium/pill shape over the page content above the bottom tab bar.
contraryEvidence: Very short toast messages (e.g. "Saved", "Copied") that naturally fit within 201px inline width do not wrap, rendering as normal single-line pills. The defect exclusively triggers on longer explanatory messages (such as achievement unlocks, sync notices, and error alerts exceeding ~25 characters).
alsoAffects: All mobile phones (<700px viewport)
iPad in portrait (wraps at 410px)
MacBook (wraps at 735px for long text)
Toasts with action buttons (data-state~="action")

Use a rounded-rect radius (r-16) when it wraps, or keep pill only for one line.

method: Traced global keydown navigation handler in js/main.js:20-28 and Money transaction row keydown in js/modules/money.js:610.
observed: In js/main.js:24, the Backspace navigation shortcut does not check if (e.defaultPrevented) return;. When a user focuses a Money transaction row and presses Backspace, money.js:610 calls e.preventDefault(); deleteEntry(t); to show the delete confirm dialog. However, main.js still intercepts the bubbling event and invokes history.back(), causing the view underneath to navigate backward to the previous page while the confirm dialog appears.
contraryEvidence: When typing inside an <input> or <textarea>, main.js returns early due to the typing check; the bug manifests whenever interactive list rows handle Backspace.
alsoAffects: Keyboard navigation in Money, list views, and delete confirmation dialogs

method: Code inspection of js/main.js (global history keydown listener) and js/modules/money.js (row-level keydown handler for entry deletion), tracing DOM event bubbling and defaultPrevented handling.
observed: In js/main.js:20-29, document listens for keydown events to implement keyboard navigation shortcuts. It checks whether the active target is typing (tag === "INPUT" || tag === "TEXTAREA" || tag === "SELECT" || isContentEditable), but fails to check e.defaultPrevented. When focus is on a transaction row in #/money/transactions, js/modules/money.js:603-611 attaches a keydown listener that catches Delete and Backspace: else if (e.key === "Delete" || e.key === "Backspace") { e.preventDefault(); deleteEntry(t); }. The row listener calls preventDefault() and opens the 'Delete this entry?' confirmation modal via KOS.ui.confirm. However, the event bubbles to document. Because the row is a DIV element, typing is false. The document listener evaluates (!e.altKey && !e.metaKey && !e.ctrlKey && e.key === "Backspace") to true and unconditionally calls KOS.back(). This causes the application to navigate back to the previous route (#/home) while the confirmation dialog opens orphaned on top of Home. Cancelling leaves the user on Home, losing their position. Furthermore, any accidental Backspace keypress when focus is on a button, checkbox, or non-input interactive element navigates the user away from their current page.
contraryEvidence: When focus is explicitly inside a standard text input, textarea, select, or contenteditable node, line 23 returns early (if (typing) return;), allowing normal text editing without triggering back navigation. The defect occurs whenever Backspace is handled on custom focusable DOM elements or pressed outside text inputs.
alsoAffects: Money transactions list
Keyboard navigation on MacBook and iPad with keyboard
Any in-page custom Backspace handler (canvas lasso, list item deletion, tree nodes)
General keyboard focus on buttons/cards

method: Inspected stacking context isolation in css/components.css:35 and css/views/governor.css:31,65.
observed: In css/components.css:35, .k-pagehead[data-state~=has-art] applies isolation: isolate. The Governor tools ⋯ menu is implemented as an inline <details> popover inside this header. The subsequent .k-gv-stage also defines an isolated stacking context (isolation: isolate) and appears later in the DOM tree. Consequently, the menu popover cannot escape the header's stacking context and is clipped/obscured behind the Stage card.
contraryEvidence: On views using the portalled KOS.ui.menu (which appends to document.body), stacking context trapping does not occur; the Governor menu was implemented as a raw inline <details> element.
alsoAffects: Governor tab ⋯ menu across Mac, iPad, and iPhone

method: Code inspection of css/components.css (.k-pagehead[data-state~="has-art"]), css/views/governor.css (.k-gv-stage, .k-gv-tools-pop), js/modules/governor-ui.js (testMenu details popover and pageHeader actions), and analysis of CSS Stacking Context hierarchy.
observed: In js/modules/governor-ui.js:205-207, testMenu() is passed as an action inside KOS.ui.pageHeader(...) and renders inside .k-pagehead. Immediately following .k-pagehead, governor-ui.js mounts .k-gv, which contains the status stage .k-gv-stage. In css/components.css:35, .k-pagehead[data-state~="has-art"] is styled with position: relative; isolation: isolate;. In css/views/governor.css:31, .k-gv-stage has position: relative; isolation: isolate;. In css/views/governor.css:65-66, .k-gv-tools-pop has position: absolute; inset-block-start: calc(100% + var(--sp-6)); z-index: var(--z-menu);. Because .k-pagehead has isolation: isolate and no z-index, it establishes a local stacking context at level 0. The following sibling .k-gv / .k-gv-stage also establishes a stacking context at level 0 and is painted later in document order, painting on top of .k-pagehead. Because z-index: var(--z-menu) on .k-gv-tools-pop cannot escape .k-pagehead's stacking context, opening the ⋯ details menu causes the popover to extend downwards over .k-gv-stage, which paints over the bottom half of the popover. Only the top ~50px spanning the gap between header and stage is visible (HP preview row cut in half, Data mode row completely hidden).
contraryEvidence: If .k-pagehead does not carry data-state="has-art" (e.g. if page art is disabled or after certain in-app transitions where data-state is omitted), isolation: isolate is not applied to .k-pagehead. In that scenario, .k-pagehead does not form a separate stacking context, allowing z-index: var(--z-menu) to paint cleanly over .k-gv-stage. The bug strictly reproduces on cold loads and views where the painted header band is active.
alsoAffects: Governor Status view on Mac, iPad, and iPad Landscape
Any popover or dropdown positioned inside .k-pagehead that overlaps adjacent isolated view containers

method: Evaluated mobile bottom navigation tab label selectors in css/layout.css:377,433 in slot 31.
observed: In css/layout.css:377, @media (max-width: 1080px) defines #cols:not([data-rail="full"]) .k-rail-label { position: absolute; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); } with specificity 1,2,0. The phone-tier rule in css/layout.css:433 uses .k-rail-label { position: static; } with specificity 0,1,0. Because the 1080px rule has higher specificity, it overrides the phone rule, clipping all tab labels into 1x1 invisible rectangles and leaving five bare kanji icons with no text labels.

method: Code inspection of css/layout.css media queries at @media (max-width: 1080px) and @media (max-width: 700px), specificity calculation of ID/class selectors, and DOM state inspection of #cols across top-level views.
observed: In css/layout.css:377 (under @media (max-width: 1080px)), #cols:not([data-rail="full"]) .k-rail-label, #cols:not([data-rail="full"]) .k-rail-count { position: absolute; inline-size: var(--hairline); block-size: var(--hairline); overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; } hides tab labels for compact rails. This selector has a specificity of (1, 2, 0). Under @media (max-width: 700px), lines 431 and 433 attempt to restore label visibility: line 431 specifies #cols[data-rail="compact"] .k-rail-label, #cols[data-tree="open"]:not([data-rail="full"]) .k-rail-label, #cols[data-tree="closed"]:not([data-rail="full"]) .k-rail-label { position: static; inline-size: auto; block-size: auto; clip: auto; overflow: visible; }, and line 433 specifies .k-rail-label { position: static; inline-size: auto; block-size: auto; clip: auto; overflow: visible; }. On an iPhone viewing Home, Productivity, Collection, or More, #cols has no data-rail attribute and data-tree is "none" or absent. Therefore, none of the selectors in line 431 match. Line 433 matches .k-rail-label, but its specificity is only (0, 1, 0), which is completely overridden by line 377's specificity of (1, 2, 0). Consequently, tab labels remain clipped into a 1x1 rect, leaving the bottom tab bar showing five bare kanji tiles (灯 学 整 蒐 余) without their English labels.
contraryEvidence: On topic pages (ref view) where a topic tree is open or closed, #cols carries data-tree="open" or data-tree="closed". In that state, line 431's #cols[data-tree="open"]:not([data-rail="full"]) .k-rail-label matches with specificity (1, 2, 0) and successfully unclips the labels. The defect is present on all non-topic pages (Home, Calendar, Money, Goals, Collection, More, etc.) where data-tree is not open/closed.

method: Traced confirmModal onKey listener in js/core/ui.js:287-289 in slot 31.
observed: In js/core/ui.js:288, function onKey(e) { if (e.key === 'Enter' && !opts.danger) close(true); } is attached to document. It does not check e.target. When focus is on the Cancel button and the user presses Enter, the document listener fires and executes close(true), resolving the dialog as confirmed instead of cancelled. This affects all non-danger confirm dialogs (End session, Turn off notifications, Disconnect GitHub, Add a copy/Open existing).
contraryEvidence: Danger dialogs set opts.danger = true, so the Enter shortcut is disabled and Enter on Cancel correctly cancels.
alsoAffects: 51+ confirm dialog call sites where danger is false

method: Code inspection of js/core/ui.js (confirmModal implementation, keydown listener on document), DOM keyboard event propagation sequence, and review of non-danger confirm modal usages across the codebase.
observed: In js/core/ui.js:288-289, confirmModal registers a global keydown handler on document: function onKey(e) { if (e.key === "Enter" && !opts.danger) close(true); } document.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);. When a non-danger confirm dialog is opened, initialFocus is placed on confirmBtn (line 305). When a keyboard or switch user presses Tab, focus moves to cancelBtn (document.activeElement === cancelBtn). When the user presses Enter on cancelBtn, the browser dispatches a keydown event with key === "Enter" on cancelBtn, which bubbles up to document before the button's native click event fires. The onKey listener intercepts the event, evaluates !opts.danger to true, and immediately calls close(true). close(true) removes the dialog overlay and triggers onYes(), executing the affirmative action. The native click event on cancelBtn is bypassed. Keyboard users intending to cancel non-danger actions (such as ending a Focus session, turning off notifications, disconnecting GitHub, resetting permissions, or leaving a session) have the action confirmed against their intent.
contraryEvidence: For dangerous confirm dialogs where opts.danger === true (e.g. "Delete this entry?"), line 288 evaluates !opts.danger to false, so onKey ignores Enter and allows the focused Cancel button to execute close(false) via its native click handler. The defect is strictly limited to non-danger confirm dialogs.
alsoAffects: All keyboard navigation on MacBook and iPad with keyboard
Accessibility switch control users
~50 non-danger confirm dialogs throughout Focus, Notifications, Code, Governor, Settings, PWA, and Collection

method: Evaluated <a class='skip-link' href='#main'> in slot 31 and traced router parse in js/core/router.js:160-166,293-294.
observed: index.html:61 defines Skip to content. Activating it sets location.hash = '#main'. KOS.router.parse('#main') splits parts to ['main']; because KOS.views['main'] is undefined, parse returns null. In onPop, if (!r) { home(); return; } executes, navigating the user away from their current page to #home instead of skipping to the main content container.
contraryEvidence: If the user is already on Home, the skip link still resets hash to #/home without moving keyboard focus to the main container.

method: Code inspection of index.html (skip-link element), js/core/router.js (hashchange listener, onPop, parse, and home fallback), and analysis of URL fragment routing.
observed: In index.html:61, the skip link is marked as Skip to content with no JavaScript click handler attached to prevent default navigation. When activated via keyboard (Enter or Space), the browser updates location.hash to "#main". This triggers the window hashchange listener in js/core/router.js:302-306, which invokes onPop({ state: history.state }). onPop passes location.hash to parse(hash) (line 293). In js/core/router.js:160-172, parse strips the leading hash and reads viewId = "main". Because "main" does not exist in KOS.views, parse returns null. Line 294 evaluates if (!r) { home(); return; } and executes home(), which immediately calls KOS.show("home"), resets lastRendered to "#/home", and replaces the current history entry. method: Inspected session logging in js/engines/flashcards.js:325-355 and reviewed session metrics in js/modules/due.js.
observed: In js/engines/flashcards.js:349, KOS.sessions.log is invoked strictly inside finish(), which only executes after the final card of the batch is answered. If the user rates cards (e.g. 25 of 30) and navigates away or closes the tab, card SRS intervals are scheduled into state.srs, but no session is logged: 0 XP is awarded, streak does not advance, and 'Today so far · Reviewed' reads 0.

method: Execution flow and session lifecycle audit of flashcard review session handling in js/engines/flashcards.js and js/modules/due.js.
observed: In js/engines/flashcards.js:297-324, during a flashcard review run, each card rating immediately executes KOS.srs.rate(c.key, r) (line 303), records in-memory counts (line 310), and persists FSRS scheduling state via store.save() (line 321). However, KOS.sessions.log(...) is NOT invoked during card rating. Instead, KOS.sessions.log is called exclusively inside finish() (lines 348-354): if (total - redoN > 0) KOS.sessions.log({ type: opts.type || "flashcards", subject: opts.sid || null, ref: opts.ref || null, metrics: { cards: total - redoN, ... } });. finish() is only reached when queue.length === 0 (line 323). If a user completes 15 out of 20 cards in a queue and navigates away, closes the tab, or switches views before finishing the final card, finish() never executes. Consequently: 1) No session log entry is created. 2) Because invariant 4a and AGENTS.md mandate that "Sessions are the sole source of streaks, XP, HP and gold", the user receives 0 XP, 0 HP, 0 gold, and no daily streak credit for their study effort. 3) In js/modules/due.js:224-236, the "Today so far" dashboard computes reviewed cards strictly by summing s.metrics.cards from KOS.sessions.today(). Because no session was logged, "Today so far · Reviewed" reads 0, directly contradicting the FSRS state that updated the 15 cards.

method: Data flow and validation event handler trace in js/modules/itdesk.js:216-236, 277-289.
observed: In js/modules/itdesk.js:216-236, the inline mark input handler for IT units validates user input on the input event: var v = inp.value === "" ? "" : Math.round(Number(inp.value)); editing.value = v === "" || !isFinite(v) || v < 0 || v > max ? "" : v; (line 223). If the user types an out-of-range mark (such as typing "459" over "45" on a 60 UMS unit), v > max evaluates to true, so editing.value is reset to empty string "", while inp.value remains "459" with bad state styling. In inp keydown listener (lines 233-236), pressing Enter executes save(r). In save(r) (lines 277-282): if (!editing || editing.value === "" || editing.value == null) { if (editing && KOS.itUnits.get(r.code).status === "done") KOS.itUnits.clearResult(r.code); editing = null; paintAll(); return; }. Because editing.value === "", the guard treats the out-of-range value as a user request to clear the mark! It executes KOS.itUnits.clearResult(r.code) without confirmation, error notice, or toast warning, silently erasing the previously saved grade and marks for that unit from state. Furthermore, clicking the "✓ Save" button (line 261) calls the exact same save(r) function and triggers the identical silent data destruction.

method: Code and architectural analysis of js/core/ui.js (scrollers(), KOS.rerender(), KOS.show()), DOM structure inspection of shell layout elements (#stage, #main, document.scrollingElement), and review of scroll restoration across synchronous views versus asynchronously/lazily populated views.
observed: Prior to commit 894a407, KOS.rerender() exclusively read and restored document.getElementById("main").scrollTop. In the desktop and iPad shell, #main has overflow: visible while its parent #stage has overflow-y: auto and acts as the true viewport scroller (on mobile shells, document.scrollingElement acts as the scroller). Consequently, #main.scrollTop was consistently 0. When KOS.show() executed, it emptied #main (main.innerHTML = ""), collapsing the content height and causing the browser to clamp #stage.scrollTop to 0. Restoring main.scrollTop = 0 left the user jumped to the top of the page. In commit 894a407 (kos-redraw-1 stopgap, js/core/ui.js:375-408), scrollers() was introduced to gather [document.getElementById("stage"), document.getElementById("main"), document.scrollingElement].filter(Boolean) and restore their scrollTop values both synchronously after KOS.show() and again in requestAnimationFrame(restore). On static, synchronously populated pages (Home, Calendar, Reminders), #stage.scrollTop is now preserved across redraws (e.g. 500px -> 500px). However, the stopgap only partially resolves the issue: on lazily batched views (e.g. Collection vaults in js/modules/medview.js:435-520, which only mount batch 1 of 60 items) or views that load data asynchronously via IndexedDB, the DOM height at the moment of both synchronous restore() and the next requestAnimationFrame is capped at the initial batch, clamping #stage.scrollTop to 0 and dropping the user back to the top (spawned as SY-19). Furthermore, horizontal scrollers and nested split-panes (e.g. Handwritten Side-by-side or Code split views) are not tracked by scrollers().
contraryEvidence: For synchronously rendered full-height pages without lazy batching or asynchronous queries (such as Home, Calendar, Reminders, and basic study ref topics), scrollers() now captures #stage.scrollTop before teardown and restores it, preventing the top-of-page jump on those routes.
alsoAffects: Collection vaults (anime, books, vn, game, mangaka) — see SY-19

Asynchronous IndexedDB views
All platforms (Mac, iPad, iPhone)

method: Code and architectural trace of js/engines/flashcards.js (queue initialization, rate(), finish(), session logging), js/modules/due.js (runSession, topic review), and js/core/ui.js (TASK_VIEWS, holdBackground).
observed: In js/engines/flashcards.js, all active review run state — queue, graduated, counts ({again: 0, hard: 0, good: 0, easy: 0}), and total — is held exclusively inside the mount closure of KOS.flashcards.mount / session (lines 280-360). On every card rating (rate(r), lines 297-324), KOS.srs.rate(c.key, r) updates FSRS scheduling parameters and calls store.save(). However, KOS.sessions.log() (the sole mechanism that awards XP, gold, and advances daily study streaks) is called exclusively in finish() upon queue exhaustion (lines 349-354). If a rerender occurs mid-session before finish(): (1) the flashcard view remounts and rebuilds its queue from scratch, restarting the learner at card 1; (2) all ratings completed before the rerender are permanently omitted from KOS.sessions.log, earning zero XP, zero gold, and zero streak credit; (3) because KOS.srs.rate() already committed FSRS schedule updates for the rated cards, presenting them again causes the user to rate them a second time within seconds, triggering FSRS short-term recalculations and corrupting scheduling stability. In commit 894a407, views "due", "ref", "review", and "personaldeck" were added to TASK_VIEWS (js/core/ui.js:356-357), causing holdBackground() to hold { background: "hard" | "soft" } redraws while on these views. However, this only suppresses background redraws; no session state persistence (state.ui.fcSession) exists, no partial batch banking (invariant 4c) is implemented, and any plain unscoped KOS.rerender() or page refresh completely wipes in-flight session credit and restarts at card 1.

method: Code and architectural audit of js/core/cloudsync.js (applyRemoteState, mergeRemoteIn, rerenderCurrent, sync event triggers) and js/core/ui.js (holdBackground, TASK_VIEWS, touch tracking).
observed: In js/core/cloudsync.js, rerenderCurrent() (lines 723-733) is invoked after every applied remote state document (applyRemoteState:775, mergeRemoteIn:495, initial link:1279). It does not compute a diff of top-level keys between the previous and incoming documents, nor do views publish subscriptions/read-sets declaring the state slices they depend on. Instead, rerenderCurrent() unconditionally calls KOS.rerender({ background: "hard" }). In commit 894a407, holdBackground("hard") (js/core/ui.js:366-372) was introduced to hold the redraw if navCur.viewId is in TASK_VIEWS, if typing() is true, if topDialog() is open, or if Date.now() - lastTouch < 45000 (retrying every 15s via bgTimer). While this prevents immediate clobbering while actively interacting, the systemic architectural defect remains: (1) cloud sync has no granular key diffing or selective view update; (2) on any view outside TASK_VIEWS (Home, Calendar, Tasks, Routines, Money, Goals, Vaults, Governor), as soon as 45 seconds elapse without a touch/pointer event, KOS.rerender() remounts the active view unconditionally, even if the synced change was completely irrelevant to that view (e.g. an achievement sweep or habit tick); and (3) on TASK_VIEWS, indefinitely holding the redraw leaves the DOM rendering stale data, creating severe write-skew risks (demonstrated by SY-18 where a held editor silently overwrites remote modifications).
contraryEvidence: Commit 894a407 stops unconditional immediate redraws during active user interaction by passing { background: "hard" } from rerenderCurrent() and enforcing a 45-second touch silence window alongside TASK_VIEWS gating.

title: Every cloud pull/merge redraws the active view unconditionally — even when nothing the view shows changed, and even while the user is mid-task
rootCauseNote: full remount used as the generic refresh for background state changes, with no busy/changed gating
fixNote: Systemic redraw policy: (1) cloudsync passes what changed (top-level keys that differ between pre- and post-merge state, cheap JSON compare per key) to KOS.rerender({changed:[...], background:true}); views declare the state keys they read (KOS.views.x.reads = ['srs','edits',...]) and are skipped when untouched. (2) A background redraw is DEFERRED while the page is 'busy': a dialog or menu open, focus in an input/textarea/contenteditable, a study engine mounted and touched in the last N minutes (flashcards/quiz/exam/japanese session/code task), pointer down, or within 30 s of the last interaction — instead show a quiet 'Updated on another device · Refresh' chip, and redraw on the next navigation. (3) For views that must refresh live, give them a refresh(changed) hook that patches in place instead of a full remount.

All non-TASK_VIEWS (Home, Calendar, Routines, Money, Goals, Vaults, Governor)

Under commit 894a407, holdBackground("soft") (ui.js:370) only holds for TASK_VIEWS, typing(), and topDialog(); because kind === "soft" excludes the 45s touch guard (which applies only to kind === "hard"), closing Daily Review while on ANY non-task view (Home, Calendar, Tasks, Routines, Money, Goals, Vaults, Governor) unconditionally and immediately remounts #main! Furthermore, the auto-open mechanism in dayreview.js:719-750 is fundamentally broken on iPad: blocked() (lines 722-729) only blocks if Focus is running, a dialog is open, in the Exam Room (#/exams/.../room), or if bootHash is non-home. But bootHash is cleared to null 1.5 seconds after launch (line 747: setTimeout(function () { maybeOpen(); bootHash = null; }, 1500)). Consequently, on iPad, whenever the user switches away and returns to the app, the visibilitychange listener (line 749: document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", ...)) triggers maybeOpen(), and blocked() returns false even if the student is actively reading a lesson or study topic! The review sheet auto-opens over the lesson, breaking Invariant 145.

method: Code and DOM teardown analysis of js/core/ui.js (KOS.rerender, KOS.show, holdBackground, typing(), scrollers()), js/core/a11y.js, and virtual keyboard behavior on mobile/iPadOS.
observed: In js/core/ui.js, KOS.rerender() delegates to KOS.show(navCur.viewId, navCur.arg, { _nav: true }). In KOS.show (lines 1572-1574), main.innerHTML = "" clears the entire DOM tree inside #main. Neither KOS.rerender nor KOS.show records an activeElement focus signature, caret position (selectionStart/selectionEnd), or active input metadata prior to teardown. Consequently, document.activeElement collapses to document.body. On iOS and iPadOS, destroying the focused input node immediately dismisses the on-screen virtual keyboard, cancels active IME composition (e.g. Japanese kanji conversion), and aborts typing mid-sentence. In commit 894a407, holdBackground(kind) (ui.js:362-368) introduced typing() checking document.activeElement tag and isContentEditable, deferring { background: "hard" | "soft" } redraws while typing is true. While this holds redraws while a field is actively focused, the architectural defect remains: (1) any plain, unscoped KOS.rerender() call without opts.background completely bypasses holdBackground and destroys active focus immediately; (2) no focus restoration mechanism exists post-render; and (3) if the user temporarily blurs the field (e.g. tapping a formatting toolbar, toggling a drawer, or pausing), typing() becomes false and the pending 15-second timer fires, remounting the view and wiping any uncommitted input text.
contraryEvidence: For background redraws carrying { background: "hard" } or { background: "soft" }, typing() actively detects focus in <input>, <textarea>, <select>, and contenteditable elements and returns "typing", deferring the redraw for 15 seconds.

method: Evaluated Collection vault lazy batch rendering in js/core/ui.js:399-404 and vault modules.
observed: Collection vaults render in 60-entry lazy batches. When KOS.rerender executes, it resets loaded batches to 60. If the user had scrolled through 200 items, the remounted DOM is too short to reach the saved scroll position, throwing the user back to the top of the vault.

method: Code inspection of js/modules/medview.js (resultsArea, BATCH = 60, IntersectionObserver sentinel), js/core/ui.js (TASK_VIEWS, scrollers(), restore()), and review of QA evaluation data (audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/r5-ipad.json).
observed: In js/modules/medview.js:23, BATCH = 60 defines the lazy rendering chunk size. In resultsArea (lines 435-520), initial results mount only batch 1 (60 cards/rows); subsequent batches are appended dynamically via an IntersectionObserver sentinel as the user scrolls down. In js/core/ui.js:356-357, Collection vault views (anime, books, vn, game, mangaka, seasonal, wishlist, shrine) are completely absent from TASK_VIEWS. When a background redraw occurs (e.g. a soft redraw from habit ticks or art loading, or a hard cloud pull after 45s of touch silence), holdBackground() permits KOS.rerender() to execute. In ui.js:402-407, scrollers() measures tops = sc.map(e => e.scrollTop) before calling KOS.show(), and runs restore() synchronously and on requestAnimationFrame(restore). However, upon remount, the vault view only renders batch 1 (60 entries). For a user who had scrolled down hundreds of entries (e.g. scrollTop 3414px in Anime, 29226px in Books), the rendered DOM height is only ~800-1200px. When restore() attempts e.scrollTop = tops[i], the browser clamps scrollTop to the maximum scrollable height (0 or near-zero). Because the scroll position is clamped to the top, the IntersectionObserver sentinel is never intersected, no further batches load, and the reader is permanently thrown back to the top of the collection.
contraryEvidence: None. Vault views are omitted from TASK_VIEWS, and the scrollers() restore mechanism lacks any capability to restore or re-hydrate lazy batches beyond the initial 60 entries.
alsoAffects: All Collection vault views (anime, books, vn, game, mangaka, wishlist, shrine)
Media browsing and filtering on Mac, iPad, and iPhone
Large media libraries (e.g. 1,880 anime titles, 2,000 books)

title: A background redraw of a Collection vault throws the reader back to the top: the lazy batches are rebuilt at 60 entries, so the saved scroll position cannot be restored
rootCauseNote: Scroll restoration assumes the remounted page is as tall as before; lazily batched lists are not, and the vault views are not held like task views.
fixNote: Either add the vault views (anime, books, vn, game, mangaka, seasonal, wishlist, shrine) to the held set, or make the vault render keep its loaded batch count in a per-visit memo (like scrollMemo) so a redraw renders up to the batch that contained the scroll position before restoring; longer term the redraw policy should diff and skip a redraw when the vault's query result did not change.
